replication_status: exact (authors' reghdfe line re-run in Stata 16 and in fixest with the review-date after_responding indicator reproduces coef, SE and N to all published digits; the spec's month-cohort gvar coding moves the TWFE by <1% for Table 6 cols 1-2 and up to 8% for Table 9 col 2, see notes)
published_source: published article, Marketing Science 42(6):1143-1161 (papers/mksc/mksc.2023.1437.pdf, p. 1151, Table 6 col High-rated); values verified Nov 2 (identical to the CA-stage LaTeX used earlier). Authors' Stata do-file (stata_replication_code.do line 65) re-run with reghdfe and reproduced in fixest with the review-level after_responding indicator: 0.00818876 (0.01210135).
notes: Table 6 col 3: High-rated hotels (rating_cat == 1); outcome exp_stars (Expedia review star rating 1-5). TWFE on review-level data assigned to hotels; FE hotel_id + exp_ymfe (year-month 1..112), cluster hotel_id, no weights, no controls. JUDGMENT CALL (PROTOCOL Nov 2 evening (d)): the review-level after_responding indicator is replaced by the month-cohort coding (reviews posted in the adoption month before the first response count as treated), so that the TWFE specs share the treatment definition of the authors' own CS panel (gname = first_response_ymfe); it moves the TWFE by <1% (Table 6 cols 1-2) to 8% (Table 9 col 2). Details: the authors' after_responding is a review-DATE indicator; 9,751 reviews posted in the adoption month before the response date are 0 for the authors but 1 under the month-cohort coding used here (gvar = first_response_ymfe, 0 = never responded). With gvar the fixest TWFE is 0.00871805 vs the authors' 0.00818876; with treat_var = after_responding run_spec.R would instead drop those rows (8,272 rows after month-level aggregation) giving 0.00887807. Within-hotel first_response_ymfe is constant; 105 cohorts (months 4..112); 1,070 never-responding hotels; no always-treated hotels (min cohort = month 4, sample starts month 1); 93 treated hotels have no reviews before their cohort month and 42 none after. reghdfe tol(1e-3) in the do-file changes nothing at 8 digits vs default tolerance.
